description: No bug — baseline clean build

Off-by-one in encode loop: loop runs `i < in_len - 1` instead of `i < in_len`, skipping the last byte. For single-byte inputs in_len-1 underflows (size_t), so the loop never executes and the output is zero-initialized garbage.
Off-by-one variant: loop starts at i=1 instead of i=0, skipping the first byte. First nibble pair is unwritten (left at zero from Wasm heap).
expected_outcome: first two hex chars are 00 instead of 68

description: Stride bug: loop increments i+=2 instead of i++, encoding only even-indexed bytes. Odd-indexed bytes are silently left as zero-initialized Wasm heap bytes.

Wrong length argument from JS: `str.length` passed to _codec_hex_encode_z instead of `bytes.length`. For pure ASCII inputs these are equal so the bug is silent; for any multi-byte UTF-8 character str.length < bytes.length, causing truncated encoding.
detected_by_test: hexEncode(é)=c3a9 / hexEncode(你好)=e4bda0e5a5bd / 4-byte emoji surrogate-pair test

description: Hardcoded in_len=1: JS always passes literal 1 to _codec_hex_encode_z regardless of input size. Only the first byte of any input is encoded. All multi-character inputs are truncated to 2 hex chars.

Output size guard removed from codec.c: `if (out_cap < need)` check is deleted. When a caller passes an undersized buffer the C loop writes past the allocation boundary, causing a Wasm linear-memory out-of-bounds trap surfaced as a pageerror event.
expected_outcome: Wasm trap / pageerror instead of negative error code
detected_by_test: undersized-buffer B003 detector / zero-cap B003 detector

description: Secondary guard removed from web_api.c: `if (out_cap == 0)` check is deleted. codec.c still guards against insufficient size, so normal usage is unaffected; only callers that explicitly pass out_cap=0 bypass the first layer of protection.
expected_outcome: returns 0 or garbage instead of negative error code

description: Both output size guards removed (codec.c AND web_api.c). Any call with an undersized buffer immediately writes out-of-bounds. Normal hexEncode() from app.js is also at risk if allocation arithmetic is ever wrong.
expected_outcome: Wasm trap on any undersized call
detected_by_test: undersized-buffer B003 detector / zero-cap B003 detector / no-trap tests for hi and long input

description: Null-pointer checks removed from codec_hex_encode. Passing a NULL input pointer with in_len>0 or a NULL output pointer with out_cap>0 causes a Wasm memory access at address 0 → immediate trap.
detected_by_test: hexEncode(A)=41 (any call that reaches the loop)

description: Wrong nibble mask for high nibble: `(b >> 4) & 0xF` changed to `(b >> 4) & 0xFF`. The shift already discards the low nibble so this is a no-op for values ≤ 0x0F, but for b ≥ 0x10 it produces indices 16–255 into the 16-byte HEX table, reading undefined memory and corrupting output.
expected_outcome: high nibble index out of range → garbage hex chars

description: Uppercase HEX table: HEX[] changed from '0123456789abcdef' to '0123456789ABCDEF'. All nibbles ≥ 0xA are uppercased. Inputs with bytes < 0xA0 in their low nibble appear unaffected; inputs with any nibble ≥ 0xA expose the bug.
Wrong out_len assignment: `*out_len = out_cap` instead of `*out_len = need`. web_api.c then null-terminates at out_cap instead of the correct position, corrupting or truncating the output string.
expected_outcome: output string is garbage-terminated or empty
